question:
Consider the following chemical reaction.

CO(g) + 2H2(g) → P

Predict the product (P) of this reaction.
solution:
The correct answer is__** CH3OH**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given reaction is:
 
 
• CO(g)+2H₂(g)→P
 
 
 
• In this reaction, **carbon monoxide (CO) reacts with hydrogen gas (H₂)** to produce methanol (CH₃OH) under suitable conditions (usually with the presence of a catalyst).
 
• Here, The predicted product (P) of the reaction is **methanol (CH₃OH)**.
 
• The balanced equation for the formation of methanol from carbon monoxide and hydrogen is **CO(g)+2H₂(g) → CH₃OH(l)**
 
• This reaction is part of the hydrogenation of carbon monoxide,
 
 
• commonly used in industrial processes such as the Catalytic Hydrogenation and Fischer-Tropsch synthesis.
